How your 9/11 memories could be wrong | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Most of us can remember exactly where we were when we heard about the September 11 terror attacks. This type of vivid recollection has been documented for other major world events too. They’re known as flashbulb memories and feel remarkably accurate, yet research suggests they can be just as unreliable as any other memory. 

So why do we trust these memories so strongly and could misremembering actually benefit us?

00:00 What is a flashbulb memory? 
00:50 Why vivid memories can be wrong 
01:40 How memory is stored and reshaped 
02:30 The science behind emotional memories 
03:20 What 9/11 studies reveal about vivid memories
04:15 Why we trust flashbulb memories so much 
05:05 President George W. Bush made a memory mistake about 9/11, researchers say
05:55 Identity, shared experiences and the future of flashbulb memories

UK accuses Israel of backing ethnic cleansing by “terrorist” settlers in West Bank | BBC News
recentItems.description:
The UK government has launched a scathing attack on Israel’s actions in the West Bank and Gaza.  The Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said ‘terrorists’ were carrying out ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, which is illegally occupied by Israel, and said they were doing so with the backing of Benjamin Netanyahu’s government. 

Mr Miliband announced sanctions on trade with settlements and declared that UK policy was now officially that Israel’s occupation of the West Bank was unlawful.  The UK announcements are the most direct condemnation of Israeli policy since it was founded as a state, and follows a summer of violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinian communities in the occupied territories. 

The UK joins 12 other countries that have announced sanctions against goods from the settlements, including France and Canada.  It comes as Israel is implementing another major expansion of settlements, with the construction of E1, a new development of 1,200 homes that will cut off Palestinians in the West Bank from East Jerusalem, which they claim as the future capital of a Palestinian state. 

The Israeli government reacted furiously to the British announcement, condemning the new Labour administration of Andy Burnham, and announcing the closure of the UK consulate in Jerusalem.  The Israeli foreign minister Gideon Saar said the UK government was “systematically working against the state of Israel” and accused Mr Miliband of telling “outrageous lies”.

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Chris Mason, Lucy Williamson and Jeremy Bowen.

recentItems.title: Palestinian parents fear for children's lives at school as settler attacks grow | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Six people, including three pupils at a boys school, have been killed in al-Mughayyir this year, in a surge of settler-related violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
 
One of them, 14-year-old Aws al-Naasan, was shot dead by a settler outside the school gates in April. Since that day, the casualties have grown alongside parents' fears.
 
The Israeli military said in a statement at the time that stones had been hurled at a car carrying "civilians including a reservist soldier", and that the reservist had got out of the vehicle and fired at suspects. Israeli media reported the reservist was later suspended from duty and an investigation launched.

All Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank are illegal under international law. Many of the small ad-hoc settler outposts that have mushroomed around al-Mughayyir are illegal under Israeli law too.
